growing_tip.body_text: Swiss Chard | → Rainbow → Giant Fordhook → 2 rows per bed spaced every 18” (45 cm) on the row → Swiss chard will stay a long time in the ground and therefore is amended with lots of compost, fresh or aged. The rule of thumb is to spread +/-1 inch (5 cm) all across the bed. When the biological activity is not optimal (cold or poor soils) add extra amendments of organic fertilizers like alfalfa meal (2-0-2) and/or pelleted chicken manure (5-3-2). | → Rotary harrow → Broadfork → 30” bed prep rake → Popping tray → Landscape fabric, staples, drip tape and fittings → Pass through with the broadfork. → Remove large debris from the bed if needed (use flail mower, rake or manually remove the large chunks). → Apply compost and/or amendments across the bed and pass with the rotary harrow at a depth of 2.5” (6 cm). Since the bed is covered with landscape fabric, it doesn’t need to be clean up with another pass of the rake. → If installing drip tape, set out 4 lines per bed and start the system. Fix leaks at point that point, if any. → Lay down landscape fabric and secured with staples every second step (5’ or 1.5 m). It needs to be really tight. → Use the popping tray to facilitate extraction and transplant the kale seedlings. Do not bury the plug (top should be even with soil level) and make sure to place them in the center of each hole. 1 person/100’bed is a good ratio for efficient workflow. → Water the bed thoroughly the first time, keeping the soil moist for the first week after transplanting. → No weeding required 2 → If problematic, control flea beetles by covering plants with anti-insect netting and mini-tunnels so the net covers the 2 beds. → Swiss Chard and Kale will benefit from monthly doses of boron and seaweed (or compost tea) applied foliarly. Plan to spray when spraying fresh beets. → Chard is harvested by cutting off 2 to 3 leaves per plant, each leaf measuring between 6” and 9” (20 and 30 cm). irrigation.body_text: → Drip tape (2 per bed) or sprinkler | → Root depth: Medium (24”-40”) → General: Average water needs, except during warm weather when more water is required to prevent wilting. We plan for 3 Swiss chard planting in the season and intend to harvest the plants over 14 weeks. This ensures continuous supply of new leaves harvested every week. Swiss chard is usually planted alongside kale, as the crops have almost identical management strategies. 1
